about: The Perfect Nations deal pipeline: every financeable Solution designed for the 195 blueprints, one line each. Built by tools/build_pipeline.py from data/state-of-nations.json, data/solutions-by-nation.json and data/more-solutions.json; do not edit by hand. Read by perfectnations.com/for-funders/.
stage: Designed: each line is designed by Perfect Nations from public data. A line becomes a mandate only when the nation asks for it.

lines.title: The People’s Jobs Certificate
lines.challenge: 16.4% of people in Portugal, about 1.8 million, live below the national poverty line: of the seven standards, livelihood is the furthest from reach.
lines.advises: Portugal should open a new series of its savings certificates whose proceeds are kept apart for work: guarantees through Banco Português de Fomento for small firms that hire and train in the towns where poverty runs deepest, and training that moves workers on low wages into better jobs. Families keep the safe return they already trust, and their savings build livelihoods in their own regions.

proof.label: of lending for more than 40,000 small firms, the largest InvestEU national compartment in Europe

lines.title: The American Table Fund
lines.challenge: The harvest is not the problem: 13.7% of American households went short of food at times in 2024 for lack of money or other resources. Since 1 October 2026 the states also carry 75% of the cost of running SNAP, the national food benefit.
lines.advises: The United States should seed a fresh food fund in every state, with state money taking the first loss and community lenders multiplying it with bank capital and New Markets Tax Credits. The fund finances grocers, food banks and the cold chains that carry food from American farms to the counties where families go short, while grocers and health plans match every SNAP dollar a family spends on fruit and vegetables, so the money a family has buys more fresh food.

proof.label: of state seed money, leveraged with $145 million more by a community lender to finance 88 fresh food retail projects

lines.title: The Solar Market Bond
lines.challenge: Nigerians use about 165 kWh of electricity a person a year, against the Living Line of 1,000: 83.5% of the electricity a person needs is missing.
lines.advises: Nigeria should dedicate its next sovereign green bond to solar mini-grids and storage for markets, clinics and homes, with private developers matching each connection and the states that open their own electricity markets served first.

proof.label: its third green bond, subscribed almost twice over

lines.title: Sunlight for Gaza
lines.challenge: Of all Palestinians, 38.3% live in Gaza, where the electricity grid has been down since October 2023.
lines.advises: Palestine should open a light fund, published in full, through which Palestinians abroad and development partners finance solar power and storage for Gaza’s hospitals, water plants, schools and homes, beginning where the need is greatest.

lines.title: Flares to Power
lines.challenge: Iraq’s grid produced 24,600 MW in September 2026, against at least 55,000 MW needed for power around the clock: 55.3% of the electricity Iraq needs is not supplied.
lines.advises: Iraq should finance the capture of the gas now burned at its oil fields and turn it into power, through project finance repaid from the electricity sold, with solar plants built on the same sites.

proof.label: senior debt for a 1.1 GW wind farm

lines.title: The Medicine Conversion
lines.challenge: Only 30% of the basic list of medicines is available to Cubans, the President of Cuba said in August 2026: 70% is not.
lines.advises: Cuba should ask its official creditors to convert part of what it owes into a medicine fund, building on the counterpart fund it already runs with France, with every purchase audited and published.

proof.label: of debt to France turned into a fund for development, health among its sectors

lines.title: Oil Behind the Sun
lines.challenge: Chadians use about 18 kWh of electricity a person a year, against the Living Line of 1,000: 98.2% of the electricity a person needs is missing.
lines.advises: Chad should invite private producers to build solar and storage plants for N’Djamena and every regional capital, with breach-of-contract cover and a reserve, financed from oil revenue, that stands behind every bill the power company owes them.

lines.title: River Power for Every Home
lines.challenge: Cameroonians use about 251 kWh of electricity a person a year, against the Living Line of 1,000: 74.9% of the electricity a person needs is missing.
lines.advises: Cameroon should finance the lines, substations and village connections that carry its river power to every home, backed by a development bank guarantee so that private lenders can lend for longer and at lower cost.

lines.title: The Blue Food Swap
lines.challenge: About 88,000 Barbadians, three in ten, are moderately or severely food insecure.
lines.advises: Barbados should make its next debt conversion a blue food swap, refinancing costly debt with guaranteed debt and binding the savings to local farms, fisheries and sea farming, so the island grows more of what it eats.

proof.label: about 30% of its ocean to be protected

lines.title: The Rift Reading Bond
lines.challenge: Four in five Kenyan children reach the end of primary school unable to read a simple text.
lines.advises: Kenya should sell a reading bond to its own citizens by phone, as it did with M-Akiba, back it with part of the revenue from its geothermal power, and release funds to schools as children learn to read.

lines.title: Solar Schools, Reading Children
lines.challenge: 56% of Indian children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2017.
lines.advises: India should put solar on the roof of every government school through its sovereign green bonds, and commit the electricity savings to reading programmes rewarded on results, as the Educate Girls impact bond first did in Rajasthan.

lines.title: Every Street Connected
lines.challenge: About 109 million Brazilians, about one in two, have no safely managed toilet at home.
lines.advises: Brazil should issue a sanitation outcome bond under its sustainable bond framework, with the return rising as each verified household is connected to a safe toilet and sewer, and pair it with the currency hedging that Eco Invest Brasil already offers foreign investors.

lines.title: Standard Tokens for Clean Kitchens
lines.challenge: About 13 million Rwandans, nine in ten, cook without clean fuel or technology.
lines.advises: Rwanda should be the first nation to pilot Standard Tokens, designed by Perfect Nations: small units of finance that citizens, investors and visitors can buy, each tied to one household’s switch to clean cooking, subject to compliance review.

lines.title: Every Child Learns
lines.challenge: Nine in ten ten-year-olds in Afghanistan cannot read a simple text.
lines.advises: Afghanistan’s partners should finance a learning outcomes fund, delivered through UN agencies and community schools, that releases money only when independent tests show children reading, and that reaches every child it can, girls included.

lines.title: Lithium for Living
lines.challenge: About 13 million Zimbabweans, three in four, have no safely managed sanitation at home.
lines.advises: Zimbabwe should commit a share of its rising lithium revenue to a sanitation fund that backs a social bond for toilets, sewers and safe homes, in the towns first and then the rural districts.

lines.title: The Copper Windfall for Learning
lines.challenge: 98% of Zambian children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2019.
lines.advises: Zambia should write a copper windfall clause into its budget, sending every kwacha earned above the budgeted copper price to a learning fund that rewards schools as children read.

lines.title: The Sanitation Exchange
lines.challenge: About 55 million Vietnamese, 55 in every hundred, have no safely managed toilet at home.
lines.advises: Vietnam should list a sanitation infrastructure fund on its newly upgraded stock market, so domestic and foreign investors can own the sewers and treatment plants its cities need, with returns tied to homes connected.
lines.instrument: FTSE Russell upgrade to emerging-market status

lines.title: The Breadbasket Guarantee
lines.challenge: About 12 million Ukrainians, 32 in every hundred, cannot always count on enough good food.
lines.advises: Ukraine should combine war-risk insurance for its farms with credit guarantees, so farmers can borrow to plant and families can count on affordable food at home while the nation rebuilds.

proof.label: for new water treatment plants
proof.source: U.S. International Development Finance Corporation, December 2024

lines.title: Cook-as-You-Go
lines.challenge: About 50 million Ugandans, almost everyone, cook without clean fuel or technology.
lines.advises: Uganda should let households cook with its clean hydropower on cook-as-you-go plans, financed by carbon credits and the Electricity Access Scale-up Project, so every new connection comes with a clean kitchen.

lines.title: Nyerere Power, Every Kitchen
lines.challenge: About 63 million Tanzanians, almost nine in ten, cook without clean fuel or technology.
lines.advises: Tanzania should turn the power of the Julius Nyerere station into clean kitchens, with a guaranteed facility like the one that brought nine banks to its railway, financing last-mile connections and electric cookers recovered through electricity bills.

lines.title: Rooftop Kitchens
lines.challenge: About 15 million Sri Lankans, 69 in every hundred, cook without clean fuel or technology.
lines.advises: Sri Lanka should finance rooftop solar and electric cooking together, through green bonds sold to Sri Lankans at home and abroad and serviced from the power each roof saves.

lines.title: Oil to Sunlight
lines.challenge: Almost every South Sudanese, 12.2 million people, cooks without clean fuel or technology.
lines.advises: South Sudan should place a fixed share of oil revenue in an account published in full, financing solar power and clean cooking in every state capital first, with development partners matching each verified connection.

proof.label: for 8.4 million tonnes of emissions cut

lines.title: A Wildlife Bond for Reading
lines.challenge: 82% of South African children could not read for meaning by the end of primary school in 2021.
lines.advises: South Africa should apply the design of its Wildlife Conservation Bond to reading: a bond with its principal protected and a return that rises as children learn to read for meaning, with an outcome funder behind it.

lines.title: The Clean Ledger Kitchen
lines.challenge: Almost every Somali, about 19 million people, cooks without clean fuel or technology.
lines.advises: Somalia should use the borrowing room its debt relief has created for a solar power and clean cooking programme, financed by concessional loans and results-based grants for each verified household and delivered through mobile money.
lines.instrument: Debt relief under the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries Initiative

lines.title: Water by Results
lines.challenge: About 14 million Senegalese, 73 in every hundred, have no safely managed drinking water at home.
lines.advises: Senegal should finance safe water at home with an outcome bond whose return rises with households connected and water tested safe, so the money follows safe water delivered rather than pipes laid.

lines.title: Carbon for Classrooms
lines.challenge: 70% of Congolese children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2019.
lines.advises: The Republic of the Congo should direct a share of its forest carbon revenue to the schools of the communities that keep the forest standing, rewarding each school as its children learn to read.

proof.label: for 8.4 million tonnes of emissions cut

lines.title: The Archipelago Reading Bond
lines.challenge: 91% of Filipino children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2019.
lines.advises: The Philippines should sell a reading bond to Filipinos at home and abroad through mobile wallets, in small amounts, to finance tutors and books for the children furthest behind.

lines.title: The Education Sukuk
lines.challenge: 80% of Pakistani children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2019.
lines.advises: Pakistan should issue an education sukuk whose proceeds open schools and train teachers where most children are out of school, with each tranche released as independent tests show children reading.

lines.title: The Diaspora Harvest Bond
lines.challenge: About 182 million Nigerians, 76 in every hundred, cannot always count on enough good food.
lines.advises: Nigeria should issue a second diaspora bond to finance storage, irrigation and warehouse receipts, so farmers can borrow against their stored grain instead of selling at harvest-time prices.

lines.title: The Hydrogen Skills Bond
lines.challenge: About 1.9 million Namibians live below US$8.30 a day, on the 2015 survey.
lines.advises: Namibia should finance a skills impact bond in which investors fund training for hydrogen, solar and wind work, and the projects and the state reward them for every Namibian placed in a lasting job.

proof.label: paid for jobs found, not for training given

lines.title: Gas to Kitchens
lines.challenge: About 33 million Mozambicans, more than nine in ten, cook without clean fuel or technology.
lines.advises: Mozambique should commit a share of future gas revenue to clean cooking at home, and finance the switch now against that revenue with development bank backing, rather than wait for first gas.

lines.title: Sun to Sanitation
lines.challenge: About 35 million Moroccans, 92 in every hundred, have no safely managed toilet at home.
lines.advises: Morocco should issue a social bond for safe toilets and wastewater treatment powered by its own clean energy, with the treated water sold to farms to help service the debt.

lines.title: The Water Guarantee
lines.challenge: About 75 million Mexicans, 57 in every hundred, have no safely managed drinking water at home.
lines.advises: Mexico should direct the World Bank credit enhancement already drawing private capital into its infrastructure toward municipal water utilities, so domestic pension savings finance safe drinking water in every state.

lines.title: Kwacha Solar
lines.challenge: Almost every Malawian, about 22 million people, cooks without clean fuel or technology.
lines.advises: Malawi should back the companies that sell solar power and clean cooking on instalments with a local-currency guarantee, so they borrow in kwacha, and connect the homes along the lines the Mpatamanga hydropower project will feed.

proof.label: Kenya’s first green bond, repaid in full

lines.title: The Vanilla Energy Fund
lines.challenge: Almost every Malagasy, about 32 million people, cooks without clean fuel or technology.
lines.advises: Madagascar should create a clean energy fund for its vanilla regions, co-financed by the buyers of its vanilla and by carbon credits from the forests that solar power and clean stoves spare from charcoal.

proof.label: for 8.4 million tonnes of emissions cut

lines.title: Water for Learning
lines.challenge: 97% of Basotho children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school, on 2016 data.
lines.advises: Lesotho should pledge a fixed share of its Highlands Water royalties to a learning trust that rewards schools as children learn to read, and let Basotho abroad add their savings through a diaspora bond.

proof.label: Treaty with South Africa
proof.source: Government of Lesotho, Government of South Africa

lines.title: The Reading Compact
lines.challenge: 62% of Jordanian children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2021.
lines.advises: Jordan should launch a learning outcomes fund in which its development partners and Jordanians abroad invest together, releasing money to schools only as children reach agreed reading levels, so every partner finances results rather than inputs.

lines.title: Hurricane-Proof Harvests
lines.challenge: About 1.6 million Jamaicans, 56 in every hundred, cannot always count on enough good food.
lines.advises: Jamaica should extend the protection of its catastrophe bond to the farm, with parametric cover for every registered farmer and fisher delivered to mobile wallets within days of a hurricane, and credit ready to replant.

proof.label: paid in full after Hurricane Melissa

lines.title: The Water Sukuk
lines.challenge: About 199 million Indonesians, 70 in every hundred, have no safely managed drinking water at home.
lines.advises: Indonesia should issue a water sukuk, ring-fenced for safe drinking water at home on every island, from piped networks to small desalination plants, building on the investor base of its green sukuk.

lines.title: Pensions for Sanitation
lines.challenge: About 28 million Ghanaians, 81 in every hundred, have no safely managed toilet at home.
lines.advises: Ghana should invite its pension funds, which already anchor the Ci Gaba Fund of Funds, into a cedi sanitation bond that finances household toilets and safe waste services, with mobile-money instalments for families and results-based support for the poorest homes.
lines.instrument: Ghana turns its pensions into venture capital

proof.label: first close of the Ci Gaba Fund of Funds, March 2026
proof.source: Small Foundation, From Vision to Validation: Ci Gaba Reaches First Close, 31 March 2026

lines.title: The Blue Livelihood Bond
lines.challenge: About 572,000 Fijians, 61 in every hundred, lived below US$8.30 a day on the 2019 survey.
lines.advises: Fiji should follow its first sovereign blue bond with one that finances the livelihoods of the sea, from fisheries and seaweed farming to coastal tourism enterprises, with cyclone cover built in so one storm cannot erase a season’s income.

lines.title: The Highland Electric Kitchen
lines.challenge: About 126 million Ethiopians, 93 in every hundred, cook without clean fuel or technology.
lines.advises: Ethiopia should turn its almost wholly renewable power into clean kitchens, financing electric cookers through monthly electricity bills and carbon credits, delivered first to households in the Productive Safety Net.

lines.title: Safe Water, Proven Home by Home
lines.challenge: About 776,000 Emaswati have no safely managed drinking water at home.
lines.advises: Eswatini should finance safe water at home the way it reached its HIV targets early: a results-based programme that releases funds for each verified household connection, built on the Mkhondvo-Ngwavuma water augmentation now under way.

proof.label: Approved 21 June 2023
proof.source: OPEC Fund for International Development, BADEA, DBSA, African Development Bank

lines.title: The Nile Reading Bond
lines.challenge: 56% of Egyptian children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2021.
lines.advises: Egypt should follow its social Eurobond with a learning-linked bond whose coupon falls if national reading scores reach an agreed target, so investors share the gain when every child reads.

lines.title: The Learning Conversion
lines.challenge: 66% of Ecuadorian children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2019.
lines.advises: Ecuador should apply the design of its Galapagos and Amazon debt conversions to learning: buy back costly bonds with cheaper, guaranteed debt and bind the savings, over many years, to teachers and reading programmes in every province.

lines.title: Cobalt for Classrooms
lines.challenge: 97% of Congolese children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2019.
lines.advises: DR Congo should pledge a share of future cobalt royalties to a learning trust that finances teachers, books and school meals, releasing each tranche as independent tests show children reading, and invite the battery makers who buy its cobalt to join as outcome funders.

lines.title: The Cocoa Classroom Fund
lines.challenge: 80% of Ivorian children could not read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2019.
lines.advises: Côte d’Ivoire should build on its debt-for-development swap with a learning fund co-financed by the companies that buy its cocoa, releasing money to schools in the cocoa regions only as children learn to read.

lines.title: The Barrio Bonds
lines.challenge: About 43 million Colombians, 81 in every hundred, have no safely managed toilet at home.
lines.advises: Colombia should let its cities issue social bonds for toilets, sewers and home upgrades in informal neighbourhoods, as Bogota did with its international green bond, and finance part of each with the land value that new transit lines create, starting with Bogota’s first metro line.

lines.title: Light for Every Hill
lines.challenge: Almost every Burundian, 14.4 million people, cooks without clean fuel or technology.
lines.advises: Burundi should finance solar mini-grids and electric cooking in its hill villages with results-based grants for each verified connection, behind the kind of political-risk cover MIGA already gives Weza Power, so private developers can build at scale.

lines.title: The Diamond Enterprise Dividend
lines.challenge: About 1.6 million Batswana live below US$8.30 a day, on the 2015 survey.
lines.advises: Botswana should commit part of its larger share of diamond sales to a sovereign fund of funds that guarantees loans to, and invests in, Batswana firms in solar power, tourism and food, so diamonds build the jobs that will outlast the mines.

lines.title: The Clean Kitchen Fund
lines.challenge: About 125 million Bangladeshis, 71 in every hundred, cook without clean fuel or technology.
lines.advises: Bangladesh should create a clean kitchen fund that lends stoves and cylinders through mobile money and sells a verified carbon credit for every household that stops cooking with wood and dung, so each switch finances the next.

proof.label: for 8.4 million tonnes of emissions cut

lines.title: The Lobito Food Corridor
lines.challenge: About 29 million Angolans, three in four, are moderately or severely food insecure.
lines.advises: Angola should set aside a share of oil revenue as first-loss capital in a corridor fund that guarantees loans to farms, mills and food traders along the Lobito railway, so local banks lend to the growers the line now reaches.

lines.title: The CASA Current
lines.challenge: People in Afghanistan use about 142 kWh of electricity a year, against the Living Line of 1,000 kWh.
lines.advises: Afghanistan should complete its stretch of the CASA transmission line with the development banks and trust funds already behind it, and take a share of the Central Asian power it carries for its own towns and clinics.

lines.title: Snowmelt to Every Tap
lines.challenge: Only 31% of people in Afghanistan use safely managed drinking water.
lines.advises: Afghanistan should invite private water operators and impact investors to build and run small piped networks in towns and villages under contracts that UN agencies and donors can monitor, so the snowmelt of the Hindu Kush reaches every home safely.

lines.title: The Clinic in Every Phone
lines.challenge: Afghanistan scores 42 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage, and women have been barred from medical training since December 2024.
lines.advises: Afghanistan should welcome telecom and pharmaceutical companies into a telemedicine and medicine partnership, so women in every province can consult women doctors at home and in the diaspora by video, and clinics never run short of essential medicines.

lines.title: The Clean Coast Compact
lines.challenge: Only 69.3% of people in Albania use safely managed sanitation, and 2.7% of city dwellers live in slums.
lines.advises: Albania should finance sewers and treatment plants for its towns and its coast with the European Investment Bank and the EBRD as it prepares to join the European Union, so the clean sea that brings its visitors is protected for the people who live beside it.

lines.title: Water Follows the Visitors
lines.challenge: Only 70.8% of people in Albania use safely managed drinking water.
lines.advises: Albania should invite the hotel groups of its coast to co-invest in the water systems of the towns that host them, under long-term supply contracts, so the safe water their guests need reaches every family in the same streets.

lines.title: The Diaspora Health Bond
lines.challenge: Albania scores 71 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Albania should offer its citizens abroad a diaspora bond for health, so their savings build modern clinics and a family doctor for every village at home and earn a fair return.

lines.title: The Beyond-Oil Venture Fund
lines.challenge: 41.8% of people in Algeria live on less than US$8.30 a day.
lines.advises: Algeria should anchor a fund of funds for young firms with part of its reserves and invite private investors alongside, so start-ups and small firms beyond oil and gas can raise capital, grow and hire.

lines.title: Every Home Connected
lines.challenge: Only 62.5% of people in Algeria use safely managed sanitation, and 13.3% of city dwellers live in slums.
lines.advises: Algeria should finance sanitation and the renewal of its informal neighbourhoods with the Islamic Development Bank and the African Development Bank, building on its large public housing programme, so every new home comes with safe sanitation.

lines.title: Sun and Sea Water
lines.challenge: Only 69% of people in Algeria use safely managed drinking water.
lines.advises: Algeria should invite its energy companies to finance and power desalination plants on the coast under long-term water purchase contracts, so the sun and gas of the Sahara bring safe water to every tap.

lines.title: The Valley Health Network
lines.challenge: Andorra scores 75 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Andorra should bring private insurers and investors into a family doctor network for every parish, linked to the specialist hospitals of its neighbours, so no resident goes without care the mountains make hard to reach.

lines.title: Apprenticeships in Every Valley
lines.challenge: Not every young person in Andorra finishes school: 93.4% complete lower secondary.
lines.advises: Andorra should invite its banks, ski resorts and hotels to offer an apprenticeship to every young person who leaves school early, so a job and a qualification are open to all.

lines.title: Schools of the Corridor
lines.challenge: Only 42% of young people in Angola complete lower secondary school.
lines.advises: Angola should finance secondary schools along the Lobito Corridor with the African Development Bank and the World Bank, each linked to the trades the railway brings, so young people stay in school for the jobs at their door.

lines.title: Oil for Clinics
lines.challenge: Angola scores 44 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Angola should ask the oil companies of its offshore fields to co-finance primary health clinics in the provinces as part of their local content commitments, so the wealth of the sea reaches the health of the interior.

lines.title: The Lobito Harvest Fund
lines.challenge: 54% of people in Angola live on less than US$4.20 a day.
lines.advises: Angola should invite private equity and impact investors into a farm fund along the corridor, financing processors and small farms that can now reach new markets by rail, so a harvest becomes an income.

lines.title: Storm-Proof Care
lines.challenge: Antigua and Barbuda scores 81 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Antigua and Barbuda should finance a hospital and clinic network built to withstand hurricanes with the Caribbean Development Bank, so care continues after every storm.

lines.title: Homes for the Hosts
lines.challenge: 2.7% of city dwellers in Antigua and Barbuda live in slums.
lines.advises: Antigua and Barbuda should invite its hotel and resort companies into an affordable housing partnership, co-financing safe homes for the workers who staff them, so no one who serves the visitors lives in a slum.

lines.title: The Barrios Upgrade
lines.challenge: Only 48.5% of people in Argentina use safely managed sanitation, and 14.5% of city dwellers live in slums.
lines.advises: Argentina should finance sewers and the upgrading of its informal settlements with the Inter-American Development Bank and the World Bank, starting with the neighbourhoods around Buenos Aires where the need is greatest.

lines.title: From Granary to Table
lines.challenge: 33.8% of people in Argentina are moderately or severely food insecure.
lines.advises: Argentina should invite its grain exporters and food companies into a partnership that finances school meals and community kitchens from what the Pampas produce, so a nation that feeds the world also feeds every child at home.

lines.title: The Peso Growth Fund
lines.challenge: 28.2% of people in Argentina live below the national poverty line.
lines.advises: Argentina should channel pension and insurance savings into a peso fund for small firms, with private investors alongside, so workshops and farms can borrow long term and hire.

lines.title: The Diaspora Venture Fund
lines.challenge: 47.4% of people in Armenia live on less than US$8.30 a day.
lines.advises: Armenia should invite its diaspora to invest in a venture fund for the regions, financing small firms, farms and guesthouses beyond Yerevan, so the families who send money home can also build businesses there.

lines.title: Care in Every Marz
lines.challenge: Armenia scores 69 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Armenia should finance family clinics and a national digital health record with the Asian Development Bank and the World Bank, so every province has a doctor close to home.

lines.title: The Tech Classroom
lines.challenge: Only 72.8% of children in Armenia can read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2019.
lines.advises: Armenia should invite its technology companies to co-finance teachers, devices and coding clubs in every primary school, so the talent behind its tech sector is found and taught in every village.

lines.title: Super for the Outback
lines.challenge: Australia scores 89 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Australia should invite its superannuation funds to finance clinics in remote and Indigenous communities through social infrastructure bonds, so the savings of the nation build care where it is hardest to reach.

lines.title: Reading in the Remote
lines.challenge: Not every child in Australia reads by the end of primary school: 90.9% can read a simple text.
lines.advises: Australia should invite its mining companies to co-finance literacy teachers and libraries in the remote schools near their operations, working with each community, so every child near the mines can read by the end of primary school.

lines.title: Every Community Connected
lines.challenge: Not every home in Australia has safe sanitation: 95.8% of people use safely managed sanitation.
lines.advises: Australia should finance water and sanitation for its remote communities through its national investment banks and housing financier, so every home has the same safe facilities as the cities.

lines.title: Doctors in Every District
lines.challenge: Austria scores 84 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Austria should finance primary care centres in every district with the Council of Europe Development Bank and the European Investment Bank, so every resident has a team of doctors and nurses close to home.

lines.title: The Second Chance Bond
lines.challenge: 14.8% of people in Austria live below the national poverty line.
lines.advises: Austria should invite private investors into a social impact bond that finances training, childcare and housing for families below the poverty line, with returns linked to the jobs they secure.

lines.title: No Plate Left Empty
lines.challenge: 4.7% of people in Austria are moderately or severely food insecure.
lines.advises: Austria should join its supermarkets and food producers in a partnership that sends surplus food to every family in need, financed and run by the companies themselves.

lines.title: The Caspian Reading Fund
lines.challenge: Only 62.5% of children in Azerbaijan can read a simple text by the end of primary school.
lines.advises: Azerbaijan should finance a reading programme in every primary school with the Asian Development Bank and the World Bank, matched by its oil fund, so the wealth of the Caspian becomes children who read.

lines.title: Local Supply, Local Jobs
lines.challenge: 35.9% of people in Azerbaijan live on less than US$8.30 a day.
lines.advises: Azerbaijan should invite the energy companies of the Caspian to buy more from local firms and farms, with supplier finance and training, so their contracts create work in every region.

lines.title: The Regional Health Partnership
lines.challenge: Azerbaijan scores 67 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Azerbaijan should open public-private partnerships for clinics and hospitals in its regions to private investors, so care beyond Baku reaches the standard of the capital.

lines.title: Care for the Family Islands
lines.challenge: The Bahamas scores 80 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: The Bahamas should finance clinics on the Family Islands with the Inter-American Development Bank and the Caribbean Development Bank, so care does not depend on a flight to Nassau.

lines.title: Every Island, a Diploma
lines.challenge: Not every young person in the Bahamas finishes school: 95.3% complete lower secondary in 2010.
lines.advises: The Bahamas should invite its resorts, banks and cruise companies to offer apprenticeships that keep young people in school to the end, so every island has a path to a diploma and a job.

lines.title: The Island Health Partnership
lines.challenge: Bahrain scores 78 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Bahrain should invite private investors into public-private partnerships for clinics and specialist care, building on its strength as a financial centre, so every resident can reach care quickly and close to home.

lines.title: Every Drop Treated
lines.challenge: Not every home in Bahrain has safe sanitation: 93.4% of people use safely managed sanitation.
lines.advises: Bahrain should invite its developers and industrial companies to co-finance the treatment and reuse of wastewater for every new district, so every home is connected and every drop is returned to use.

lines.title: The Delta Sanitation Drive
lines.challenge: Only 37.3% of people in Bangladesh use safely managed sanitation.
lines.advises: Bangladesh should finance safe toilets and faecal sludge treatment for its cities and towns with the Asian Development Bank and the World Bank, so the growth of its cities brings health, not disease.

lines.title: Threads of Literacy
lines.challenge: Only 48.8% of children in Bangladesh can read a simple text by the end of primary school.
lines.advises: Bangladesh should invite its garment exporters and their international buyers to co-finance reading programmes in the schools of the families who work in the factories, so the industry that clothes the world also teaches its children to read.

lines.title: The Community Clinic Fund
lines.challenge: Bangladesh scores 54 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Bangladesh should invite impact investors into a fund that finances community clinics and health workers, repaid through insurance premiums collected by mobile money, so primary care reaches every village.

lines.title: The Health Dividend
lines.challenge: Barbados scores 82 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Barbados should build on its debt-for-health conversion with the Inter-American Development Bank, so the savings finance a family doctor and a health record for every household.

lines.title: The Blue Enterprise Fund
lines.challenge: In the last poverty survey of Barbados, now dated, 82.5% of people lived above the national poverty line.
lines.advises: Barbados should invite private investors into a blue economy fund for fishers, boat builders and small tourism firms, so the sea that surrounds the island becomes a livelihood for more of its people.

lines.title: Every Child, a Reader
lines.challenge: 97% of young people in Barbados complete lower secondary school, and reading is not yet measured.
lines.advises: Barbados should invite its hotels and international business firms to co-finance a national reading assessment and apprenticeships for every school leaver, so the nation knows that every child can read and has a path to work.

lines.title: Modern Clinics for Every Region
lines.challenge: Belarus scores 80 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Belarus should finance the modernisation of its regional clinics and hospitals with the Eurasian Development Bank, so care outside Minsk matches the capital.

lines.title: Clean Water, Clean Industry
lines.challenge: Belarus still falls short of safe water for all: 93.1% use safely managed drinking water.
lines.advises: Belarus should invite its food and industrial companies to co-finance water treatment for the towns around their plants, under long-term stewardship contracts, so every home has safely managed water.

lines.title: The Regional Enterprise Fund
lines.challenge: 3.5% of people in Belarus live below the national poverty line.
lines.advises: Belarus should open a fund for small firms in its regions to private investors, so workshops, farms and services beyond the capital can borrow and hire.

lines.title: Care Close to Home
lines.challenge: Belgium scores 86 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.

lines.title: Reading at Every Desk
lines.challenge: Not every child in Belgium reads by the end of primary school: 91.5% can read a simple text.
lines.advises: Belgium should invite its employers and publishers into a reading partnership that funds tutors and libraries in the schools where reading lags, so every child reads by the end of primary school.

lines.title: The Full Plate Bond
lines.challenge: 8.1% of people in Belgium are moderately or severely food insecure.
lines.advises: Belgium should invite private investors into a social impact bond that finances food banks, school meals and cooking skills, with returns linked to fewer families going hungry.

lines.title: The Barrier Reef Enterprise Fund
lines.challenge: 52% of people in Belize live below the national poverty line.
lines.advises: Belize should open a blue and green enterprise fund to impact investors, building on its marine conservation debt swap, so fishers, guides and small tourism firms can borrow and grow while the reef is protected.

lines.title: Harvest Contracts
lines.challenge: 45.5% of people in Belize are moderately or severely food insecure.
lines.advises: Belize should invite its sugar, citrus and banana companies into contract farming with small growers, with guaranteed purchase and seeds on credit, so every farm family can grow more food and earn more from it.

lines.title: Care in Every District
lines.challenge: Belize scores 70 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Belize should finance clinics in its rural districts with the Caribbean Development Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank, so care does not depend on a journey to the city.

lines.title: The Lagoon Sanitation Plan
lines.challenge: Only 16.4% of people in Benin use safely managed sanitation, and 64% of city dwellers live in slums.
lines.advises: Benin should finance safe sanitation for Cotonou and its lagoon towns with the African Development Bank and the World Bank, with drainage and treatment that protect the homes of the poorest, so cities grow healthy.

lines.title: Water for Every Village
lines.challenge: Only 17.7% of people in Benin use safely managed drinking water.
lines.advises: Benin should invite private operators and investors to build and run village water networks under performance contracts with the state, so a safe tap stands in every village and is kept working.

lines.title: Cotton for Classrooms
lines.challenge: Only 27.9% of young people in Benin complete lower secondary school.
lines.advises: Benin should invite its cotton and cashew companies to co-finance lower secondary schools in the farming regions they buy from, so the children of every grower stay in school.

lines.title: School Through the Valleys
lines.challenge: Only 56.6% of young people in Bhutan complete lower secondary school.
lines.advises: Bhutan should finance lower secondary schools and boarding places in its remote valleys with the Asian Development Bank, so every young person can finish school without leaving the mountains behind.

lines.title: The Dam Dividend
lines.challenge: Only 65.6% of people in Bhutan use safely managed drinking water.
lines.advises: Bhutan should invite its hydropower companies to co-finance safe drinking water for the valleys below their dams, from a share of the power they export, so the rivers that light the region also serve every home.

lines.title: The Mountain Health Bond
lines.challenge: Bhutan scores 69 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Bhutan should invite private investors into a health bond that finances clinics and telemedicine across the mountains, with returns linked to the people reached, so care follows the people wherever they live.

lines.title: Lithium for Livelihoods
lines.challenge: 44.7% of people in Bolivia live below the national poverty line.
lines.advises: Bolivia should require the companies that develop its lithium to buy from local firms, train local workers and co-finance small businesses in the communities of the salt flats, so the metal of the future builds livelihoods today.

lines.title: Clinics of the Altiplano
lines.challenge: Bolivia scores 67 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Bolivia should finance primary care clinics across the highlands and lowlands with the Inter-American Development Bank and CAF, so care reaches every community in its own language.

lines.title: The Stay-in-School Bond
lines.challenge: Only 88.5% of young people in Bolivia complete lower secondary school.
lines.advises: Bolivia should invite impact investors into an education outcomes bond that finances transport, meals and tutors, with returns linked to more young people completing school, so no one leaves too early.

lines.title: Family Medicine for All
lines.challenge: Bosnia and Herzegovina scores 64 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Bosnia and Herzegovina should finance family medicine teams and clinics in every municipality with the Council of Europe Development Bank and the EBRD, so every resident has a doctor close to home.

lines.title: Clean Heat at Home
lines.challenge: Only 65% of people in Bosnia and Herzegovina cook with clean fuels and technology.
lines.advises: Bosnia and Herzegovina should invite private investors into a clean heating and cooking fund that replaces wood and coal stoves with efficient electric and district heat, repaid from the energy saved, so every home breathes clean air.

lines.title: The Diaspora Supply Chain
lines.challenge: 16.9% of people in Bosnia and Herzegovina live below the national poverty line.
lines.advises: Bosnia and Herzegovina should invite its exporters and the companies of its diaspora to buy from small local suppliers with supplier finance and training, so their orders create work in every town.

lines.title: Contracts for Cattle and Crops
lines.challenge: 52% of people in Botswana are moderately or severely food insecure.
lines.advises: Botswana should invite its supermarket chains and beef exporters into contract farming with small farmers, with guaranteed purchase and inputs on credit, so more food is grown and sold at home.

lines.title: Diamonds for Readers
lines.challenge: Only 49.2% of children in Botswana can read a simple text by the end of primary school in 2011.
lines.advises: Botswana should finance a reading programme in every primary school with the African Development Bank and the World Bank, matched by its diamond revenues, so the wealth under the ground becomes children who read.

lines.title: The Kalahari Health Partnership
lines.challenge: Botswana scores 60 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Botswana should invite private investors and medical schemes into partnerships for clinics in its rural districts, so care in the Kalahari matches care in Gaborone.

lines.title: The Literate Child Pact
lines.challenge: 48% of children in Brazil could not read a simple text by the end of primary school, in the last data, from 2013.
lines.advises: Brazil should finance its national commitment to literate children with the Inter-American Development Bank and the World Bank, starting in the North and Northeast, so every child reads by the end of primary school.

lines.title: Family Farms, Big Buyers
lines.challenge: 20.6% of people in Brazil live on less than US$8.30 a day.
lines.advises: Brazil should invite its food and agribusiness companies to buy from family farms with supplier finance and technical support, so the farms that feed the nation also earn a living.

lines.title: The Unified Health Partnership
lines.challenge: Brazil scores 84 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Brazil should open public-private partnerships for hospitals and clinics in its underserved states to private investors, so the national health system reaches every patient with the same quality.

lines.title: Energy for Health
lines.challenge: Brunei scores 84 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Brunei should invite its energy companies to co-finance primary care and screening for chronic illness in every district, so the wealth of its oil and gas keeps every citizen well.

lines.title: Clinics for the Countryside
lines.challenge: Bulgaria scores 73 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
lines.advises: Bulgaria should finance primary care clinics and mobile teams for its rural regions with the European Investment Bank and the Council of Europe Development Bank, so care in the villages matches care in Sofia.

lines.title: The Regional Jobs Fund
lines.challenge: 21.2% of people in Bulgaria live below the national poverty line.
lines.advises: Bulgaria should invite private investors into a fund for small firms and social enterprises in its poorest regions, so the families below the poverty line find work close to home.

lines.title: Reading First, Then Code
lines.challenge: Only 81.8% of children in Bulgaria can read a simple text by the end of primary school.
